On Tuesday, 21 May 2024, Russia's military began drills involving tactical nuclear weapons that authorities had announced on 6 May, in an apparent warning to senior Western officials who had spoken about deeper involvement in the war in Ukraine.[{n}] It was the first time Russia had publicly announced drills involving tactical nuclear weapons, although its strategic nuclear forces exercise regularly.[{n}] According to a Defense Ministry statement, the first stage envisioned 'practical training in the preparation and use of non-strategic nuclear weapons,' including nuclear-capable Kinzhal and Iskander missiles.[{n}] The maneuvers took place in the Southern Military District, comprising Russia's southern regions including the border with Ukraine, Crimea — annexed from Ukraine in 2014 — and four Ukrainian regions Russia annexed in 2022 and partially occupies.[{n}] The ministry said the drills responded to 'provocative statements and threats of certain Western officials regarding the Russian Federation.'[{n}]
Announcement of the 2024 tactical nuclear drills

The Russian Defense Ministry announced on 6 May 2024 that drills involving non-strategic nuclear weapons would be held in response to 'provocative statements and threats of certain Western officials regarding the Russian Federation.'[{n}] When the exercises began on 21 May, the ministry said the first stage envisioned 'practical training in the preparation and use of non-strategic nuclear weapons,' including nuclear-capable Kinzhal and Iskander missiles, conducted in the Southern Military District.[{n}]
Succession and elections after Raisi's death (2024)

The death of President [[ebrahim-raisi|Ebrahim Raisi]] in May 2024 obliged Iran's leadership to hold a presidential election within 50 days as mandated by the Constitution, presenting the political establishment with a decision it did not want to make.[{n}] For decades Iran's leaders had pointed to high voter turnout as proof of the Islamic Republic's legitimacy, but turnout had fallen sharply — from more than 60 percent in the 2016 parliamentary elections to 42 percent in 2020 and just under 41 percent in March 2024, despite official vows that the figure would rise.[{n}] Supreme Leader [[ali-khamenei|Ali Khamenei]] faced two risky options: opening the contest to all candidates from hard-liners to reformists, risking a competitive election with an unwanted outcome, or repeating his practice of blocking reformists and even moderate loyal opposition figures, risking still lower turnout that would read as a stinging rebuke of his increasingly authoritarian state.[{n}]

Following the death of President [[ebrahim-raisi|Ebrahim Raisi]] in May 2024, Khamenei faced a constitutionally mandated presidential election within 50 days and two options, each carrying risk.[{n}] He could open the field to all candidates from hard-liners to reformists, risking a competitive contest that might take [[iran|Iran]] in a direction he did not want, or he could again disqualify reformist rivals and even moderate, loyal opposition figures, risking the embarrassment of still lower turnout interpreted as a rebuke of his increasingly authoritarian state.[{n}]

Raisi's death in May 2024 triggered a constitutional requirement that [[iran|Iran]] hold a presidential election within 50 days, forcing the political establishment into a decision it had sought to avoid amid years of plummeting voter turnout.[{n}] Supreme Leader [[ali-khamenei|Ali Khamenei]] was left choosing between an open, competitive contest and a further round of candidate disqualifications that risked record-low participation.[{n}]

During a May 2024 appearance on Fox News, Maher asserted that in some cases transgenderism is just 'a TikTok challenge that got out of hand.'[{n}] He argued that the United States had become an 'outlier' compared with other Western nations, noting that European countries were moving away from measures such as puberty blockers for children.[{n}] Maher also drew a distinction between liberalism and 'woke,' saying: 'Liberalism is not the same thing as woke, woke they would like to think they're an extension of liberalism, they're not, I'm an old school liberal, it's very often the opposite,' adding that 'they think they're going so far in the right direction and it actually turns out that they're in the wrong direction and they've actually reversed it.'[{n}]

The 22 May 2024 edition, titled 'Trump's Defense Rests, but the Info War Accelerates,' covered news items from Tuesday, 21 May, with commentary from [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]], [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] and [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]].[{n}] Items included the close of the defense case in [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s New York hush money trial, [[norway|Norway]]'s declaration that it would arrest Israeli leaders on an [[international-criminal-court|ICC]] warrant, the liquidation of the [[northeast-gasoline-supply-reserve|Northeast Gasoline Supply Reserve]], [[klaus-schwab|Klaus Schwab]]'s step-back from the [[world-economic-forum|World Economic Forum]], the widening Slovak probe into the shooting of [[robert-fico|Robert Fico]], the Georgia primary wins of [[fani-willis|Fani Willis]] and [[scott-mcafee|Scott McAfee]], and the [[protecting-americans-in-the-idf-act|Protecting Americans in the IDF Act]].[{n}] Bonus items covered Russian tactical nuclear drills, Iran's post-Raisi election dilemma, and [[bill-maher|Bill Maher]]'s remarks on transgenderism.[{n}]
